disease_label_per_paper: Antibiotic-refractory left upper lobe lung abscess with initial percutaneous drainage failure requiring larger catheter exchange
presentation_summary: A 42-year-old man presented with persistent fever and left chest pain for two weeks.
Chest radiograph showed diffuse consolidation of the left lung.
Chest CT showed a large left upper-lobe abscess with an air-fluid level and extensive consolidation of the whole left lung.
He was diagnosed with severe pneumonia with a lung abscess and was treated empirically with meropenem and vancomycin.
After five days of antibiotics there was no satisfactory clinical response; CT-guided drainage with a 10-Fr pigtail catheter removed 42 mL of pus.

The small catheter clogged the next day, residual abscess content remained, right-lung pneumonia developed after suspected aspiration of abscess material, and respiratory failure required ventilation and later tracheostomy.
A 28-Fr catheter exchange under lung isolation drained 650 mL over eight days; pus culture grew Prevotella buccae, Streptococcus anginosus, and Fusobacterium necrophorum.

actual_treatment.name: empiric meropenem plus vancomycin for severe pneumonia with lung abscess
CT-guided drainage with 10-Fr pigtail catheter after five days of antibiotics
larger 28-Fr catheter exchange under general anesthesia and one-lung ventilation
antibiotics de-escalated to sulbactam-ampicillin after pus culture; later oral garenoxacin until day 35

outcome_follow_up.description: Free from ventilator support on day 5 after catheter exchange.
Drainage catheter removed on day 18 after exchange.
Discharged without complications on day 40 after catheter exchange.
Seven-month CT showed complete cure with only a small residual thin-walled cavity.
